findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 44 mm is observed in the head of the pancreas. The common bile duct is interrupted by the tumor, suggesting invasion. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the portal vein, suggesting potential invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. Contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric artery, celiac artery, and common hepatic artery is observed, indicating possible invasion. Prominent soft tissue shadows around the vessels raise suspicion of extrapancreatic nerve plexus invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. No lymph node metastases are present. No other evident metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH1 (Common bile duct invasion)
DU0 (No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum)
S1 (Serosal invasion)
RP1 (Retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV1 (Portal vein contact of more than 180°, suggesting potential invasion)
A1 (Contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric artery, celiac artery, and common hepatic artery, indicating possible invasion)
PL0 (No invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (Extrapancreatic nerve plexus invasion)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the local invasion factors, the T classification is T4, as there is invasion of the common bile duct, serosal invasion, retropancreatic tissue invasion, and contact of more than 180° with major vessels, indicating a high degree of local invasion.

N classification: N0, as there are no regional lymph node metastases.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There are no distant metastases present, such as to non-regional lymph nodes or distant organs.

M classification: M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the resectability classification is Resectable (R), as there are no distant or non-regional metastases.

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T, N, and M categories, the overall stage is Stage IIA.
